prompt:
Location plate. The waterfront edge of Tenochtitlan where the great causeway
leaves the city, night, 1520. Camera is elevated on a rooftop terrace one block
back inside the city, looking down and out across an open waterfront quay to the
mouth of the causeway, which runs diagonally away toward the upper right and
recedes to a vanishing point at the horizon. No people anywhere in frame.

GROUND PLAN — READ THIS FIRST, IT GOVERNS THE WHOLE SHOT
There are three distinct zones and they must not merge:
1. CITY BLOCK (foreground, lower frame): flat lime-plastered rooftops and a
   stretch of stone street below, one full block back from the water.
2. THE QUAY (midground, crossing the frame): a broad open paved road running
   PERPENDICULAR to the causeway, left to right across the frame along the whole
   lake edge. It is 20 meters wide, completely clear, and separates every
   building in the city from the water. Nothing is built on it.
3. THE CAUSEWAY: launches out of the quay at a T-junction and runs off on a
   three-quarter diagonal to the upper right across open water. It is 40 feet wide! Not narrow. It is as wide as the street that it T-junctions with
No building stands at the mouth of the causeway. No building comes closer than
20 meters to the water's edge. Nothing frames, flanks, brackets or overhangs the
causeway head. The causeway begins in open ground and the transition is a plain
stone threshold — no gate, no arch, no gateposts. The buildings form a set-back
wall of architecture facing the water across the empty quay, and the causeway
runs out from that open space alone.

THE CAUSEWAY — CONSTRUCTION AND SCALE
Scale is critical and must read correctly. The paved deck is about 22 meters
across — as wide as seven adult men laid head to toe end to end. Make it twice as wide as you want to.  The deck surface
sits roughly the height of one adult man above the water line. Deck surface is
close-laid irregular flat stones, worn smooth in the center where traffic has
passed, rougher at the edges. Both flanks are faced with cut stone blocks capped
by a flush stone edge course, with vertical dressed-stone pier posts set into the
facing at regular intervals along the length. Below the facing, a wide apron of
heaped rounded boulders and cobble riprap slopes down into the water on both
sides. The road runs dead straight, unbroken, no bridge gaps, no parapet, no
railing. Monumental engineering, enormous against the human scale stated above.
From this raised angle the full width of the deck is clearly visible as a broad
flat surface, not a thin line.

ARCHITECTURE — THE CITY EDGE
Low stone buildings faced with lime stucco in cream and warm grey, wide sloping
talud bases, plain rectangular doorways with square lintels, painted horizontal
bands of dark red, ochre and turquoise stepped-fret patterning below the
rooflines, the paint chalky and sun-faded. Every roof is a flat lime-plastered
terrace with a low parapet. Nothing above two stories. Mesoamerican construction
only, hand-cut stone and lime plaster throughout. Doorways stand open and black.
The buildings sit in an unbroken line along the far side of the quay, their
fronts facing the water, well back from it.

LIVED-IN DRESSING
Modest signs of ordinary life kept tight against the building fronts on the far
side of the quay: rolled reed mats stood against a wall, waist-high clay water
jars beside two doorways, a tipped basket, broken pottery sherds, a coil of rope,
bundled firewood. Sparse and scattered. The center of the quay and the causeway
mouth stay completely clear and empty.

WATER
Lake Texcoco, wide and open on both sides of the causeway and running along the
full length of the quay edge, shallow and dark. Small low ripples and a slight
swell, no waves breaking, no whitecaps. The water surface is near-black with a
thin cold sheen picking out the ripple tops, and a soft broken reflection of the
causeway's stone flank running along the waterline.

LIGHTING
Moonless night. The sky is pure black — cloud cover so heavy and the night so
deep that the sky renders as a flat black void above the horizon with no cloud
form, no cloud edge, no tonal variation and no stars. A single hard cool source
at 8500K sits high and roughly three-quarters behind the causeway, nearly
backlighting the scene: a cold bright line along the causeway's stone edge
course, the tops of the pier posts, the upper faces of the boulder riprap, the
roof parapets, the top edges of the talud bases, and a broad cool wash raking
across the open paving of the quay. Faces of walls turned away go near-black. The
horizon reads as a hard line where the faintly lit water meets the black sky. All
light in frame is this one cool source — no fire, no torches, no lamps, no lit
doorways or windows anywhere. Color lives in what the light rakes across: chalky
cream stucco going blue-grey, dark red and turquoise bands reading almost as
tone, warm brown surfacing in the stone only where the edge light clips it.

ATMOSPHERE
Mild dry night air, no rain, no wet ground, no fog. Haze 15%, just enough to
soften the last third of the causeway before it reaches the horizon.

CAMERA
Locked-off elevated wide. Camera height 7 meters, standing on a rooftop terrace
one full block back from the water. 63 degree FOV. Tilted DOWN roughly 20 degrees
so the frame is dominated by the ground plane — foreground rooftop and street,
then the open quay, then the causeway running away on its diagonal. The horizon
line sits high, in the upper quarter of the frame, not centered. The shot looks
down onto the geography, reading it like a map, not out toward the distance.
Camera offset to the camera-left side so the causeway leaves frame on a diagonal
to the upper right. Rectilinear, no perspective distortion. Foreground and
midground sharp, far distance soft.

STYLE
Photorealistic cinematic film still, natural film grain, restrained contrast,
naturalistic color, matte finish, 4K, 16:9. Original photoreal rendering with
real stone grain, real plaster texture and real depth. Clean frame, no text, no
lettering, no subtitles.

NEGATIVE
No buildings at the causeway mouth, no buildings at the water's edge, no walls
flanking the causeway, no structures overhanging the water, no gateway, no arch,
no gateposts, no narrow alley or corridor effect, no eye-level or ground-level
camera, no horizon in the center of frame. No people, no figures, no silhouettes,
no animals, no boats, no canoes, no fire, no torches, no lit windows, no moon, no
stars, no clouds, no rain, no fog, no smoke, no bridges, no gaps in the road, no
railings, no banners.
